title: The Principal a Certificate of Deposit Carries Into a New Term
content:
The balance a certificate shows on the day a new term is recorded is not always the principal the new term is priced on. Where the certificate saw movement in the days after its maturity, the principal carried in is measured against that movement.

## The measure

The principal carried into the new term is measured as follows: where a deposit was posted to the certificate in the days after its maturity and the rate of the term that ended stood above the tier's published standard interest rate, it is the balance standing on the certificate less every deposit posted in those days; where principal was taken out in the days after maturity and no deposit was posted there, it is the balance standing on the certificate together with every such withdrawal; otherwise it is the balance standing on the certificate.

## Input, judgement, output

**Input.** The balance standing on the certificate of the Certificates of Deposit line; the deposits posted to it in the days after its maturity; the principal taken out of it in those days; the rate the term that ended carried, set against the standard interest rate the tier publishes.

**Judgement.**

| Deposits in the days after maturity | Principal taken out in those days | The ended term's rate against the tier's published standard rate | Principal carried into the new term |
|---|---|---|---|
| one or more | any | above it | the balance, less every deposit posted in those days |
| one or more | any | at it or below it | the balance |
| none | one or more | any | the balance, together with every such withdrawal |
| none | none | any | the balance |

**Output.** One sum in USD, on which the new term is priced.

## Worked readings, on hypothetical figures

A certificate stands at 104000.00 USD. In the days after its maturity a deposit of 9000.00 USD was posted, and the term that ended carried 4.05 percent against a published standard rate of 3.97 percent for the tier. The rate stood above the published figure and a deposit was posted, so the principal carried in is 104000.00 less 9000.00, or 95000.00 USD.

Had the term that ended carried 3.97 percent, equal to the published figure rather than above it, no grade of the first kind would be met and, a deposit having been posted, the principal carried in would be the balance itself, 104000.00 USD.

A certificate standing at 61000.00 USD from which 4000.00 USD was taken out in the days after maturity, with no deposit posted there, carries in 61000.00 together with 4000.00, or 65000.00 USD.

A certificate that saw neither a deposit nor a withdrawal in those days carries in exactly the balance standing on it.
